title: Personal history; family background
description: The interviewer begins by asking Hope Maddox about her personal history, including her full name, date and place of birth, and her parents' names, birth dates, and origins. Maddox provides details about her mother's maiden name and her parents' marriage.

title: Parents' occupations; father's family
description: Maddox discusses her mother's work as a seamstress and in a laundry before her marriage, and mentions her father was from an old family. She also shares a story about her great-grandfather ending up in a German prison.

title: Siblings; husband; children
description: The interviewer asks Maddox about her siblings, and she names her oldest brother. She then talks about her husband, Clyde, and his health issues, and states that she has no children.

title: Education; early work experiences
description: Maddox briefly mentions her high school education and then recounts her early work experiences, including working as a coach while still in school.

title: Radio work experiences
description: Maddox shares stories from her time working in commercial radio, including a unique three-way conversation.

title: Needlework skills; hobbies
description: The conversation shifts to Maddox's hobbies and skills, with a focus on her various needlework projects like tatting and needlepoint.

title: Community involvement; rural life
description: Maddox talks about her involvement in trustee associations and her preference for rural living, mentioning her husband's love for hunting.

title: Childhood comparison; women's work
description: The interviewer asks Maddox to compare her childhood with that of children today. Maddox then discusses her experiences as a woman in the workforce, including pay discrimination during World War II.

title: Technology's impact on work; reflections
description: Maddox reflects on how the introduction of computers changed her job and her feelings about the challenges and rewards of work, both in the past and present.

title: Gardening and canning; relaxation, television and reading
description: Hope Maddox talks about her ongoing canning and garden work and her liking for homegrown beans. She then describes how she relaxes, including sitting outside with her cat Isabel, and names science fiction, movies, and books as favorite pastimes.

title: Marriage and early married life; Depression; buying property and building a house
description: She answers questions about her early married life and whether she worried about her husband. She says steady work meant they barely felt the Depression, and describes buying mining buildings and acreage, building a house, and their firm rule against going into debt.

title: Driving; wartime work; women's jobs at Bunker Hill
description: Hope recalls learning to drive and then describes the war years, when she went to work at the Bunker Hill mine as women took over men's jobs. She notes that many women were later expected to give those jobs up, and that new equipment has since lightened the work.

title: Attitudes toward debt; work ethic; birth control and family responsibility
description: She contrasts her generation's avoidance of debt with modern families' reliance on credit. She stresses the value of work throughout her life, recounts her New York family background and wartime losses, and voices strong support for birth control and responsible parenting.

title: Poverty, welfare and the value of work; closing and release form
description: Hope recounts a story of a woman on welfare and expresses frustration about food stamps, arguing that any work is better than the dole. She reflects on her sister's good fortune, and the interviewer closes by explaining the release form and confidentiality choices before she signs.
